newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan retail sales mixed, consumers stay cautious.
newsitem.headline: Japan retail sales mixed, consumers stay cautious.

text.p: Mixed results for Japan's retail sales in August showed that consumers were still cautious amid a slow economic recovery and lingering fears of a food poisoning epidemic that struck the nation this summer.
Sales at Japanese chain stores fell 0.2 percent from a year ago to 1.4 trillion yen ($12.7 billion), the Japan Chain Stores Association said on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, sales at department stores in Japan increased 1.2 percent year-on-year in August to 579.3 billion yen ($5.26 billion), the Japan Department Stores' Association said.

"It can be said from looking at the figures that consumption is not totally bad, but still not very strong," said Susumu Takeuchi, an analyst at Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics.
He said that sales at chain stores continued to be affected by the O-157 bacteria food-poisoning epidemic, which has killed 11 people and made thousands ill so far.
The chain store association also noted that sales of fresh food continued to be sluggish in August as consumers avoided certain vegetables and beef products thought to be linked to the epidemic.

Mike Allen, an analyst at Baring Securities Inc, said that the slight increase in department stores sales in August was mainly due to an extra weekend, which especially helped sales of clothing, as well as boosted demand from corporate customers.
The department stores association said that sales of autumn clothing started out fairly well in August.
However, Allen also pointed out that many department stores appeared to have missed the opportunity to profit in the bargain season during August due to the excessive reduction of inventories.
Analysts said that retailers' sales will likely continue to be relatively sluggish as consumers remain cautious in light of not-so-strong economic conditions.
"The consumers have become very picky and highly value-conscious," said Allen.
The rapid expansion of selling areas will also be a significant negative factor, analysts said.
Allen said that the retailers' selling area is expected to grow four percent in the next year.
